SUPREME COURT OF THE UNITED STATES

No. 17-1011

BUDHA ISMAIL JAM, ET AL., PETITIONERS v.
INTERNATIONAL FINANCE CORPORATION

ON WRIT OF CERTIORARI TO THE UNITED STATES COURT OF APPEALS FOR THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA CIRCUIT

[February 27, 2019]

CHIEF JUSTICE ROBERTS delivered the opinion of the Court.

The International Organizations Immunities Act of 1945
grants international organizations such as the World Bank and the World Health Organization the "same im-munity from suit ... as is enjoyed by foreign govern- ments." 22 U.S.C. §288a(b). At the time the IOIA was enacted, foreign governments enjoyed virtually absolute immunity from suit. Today that immunity is more lim-ited. Most significantly, foreign governments are not
immune from actions based upon certain kinds of commer-cial activity in which they engage. This case requires us to determine whether the IOIA grants international organi-zations the virtually absolute immunity foreign govern- ments enjoyed when the IOIA was enacted, or the more limited immunity they enjoy today.
